prompt: Which of the following is an example of an advertising agency being involved in service marketing rather than institutional marketing:
choices: Creating a certain public image for the advertising agency
Communicating the ad agency's mission statement on its web site
explanation: Performing intangible activities for clients. Service marketing involves an advertising agency performing intangible activities that satisfy a client's wants and needs. For example, developing ideas for a promotional campaign is one intangible activity that an advertising agency does for its clients. The focus of institutional marketing has to do with promoting the business rather than any goods or services it sells. An advertising agency that creates a certain image for itself, communicates its mission statement on its web site, and providing shareholders with financial information are activities that encompass institutional marketing.

prompt: Tim and Dan want to start a specialty advertising business. Their main problem is accumulating enough money to pay start-up costs as well as initial operating expenses. What legal structure of business ownership is best for Tim and Dan?
explanation: Corporation. By starting a corporation, Tim and Dan can sell stock to raise the necessary capital to cover business expenses. By owning the majority of the stock themselves, they can still control the specialty advertising business. A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person. A major disadvantage of a partnership is that the capital available is limited to the partners' resources, so partnership is not the best option for Tim and Dan. A franchise owner buys the right to sell the goods or services of the parent company. Franchises are business ownership options rather than legal business structures.

prompt: A written business report should have clarity so that it will be
explanation: Easy to understand. Clarity is expressing thoughts in a clear manner. Clarity is very important in business communication because it prevents misunderstandings. The meaning of the message is clear rather than being open to interpretation. Having clarity does not ensure that communication will be impressive. The length of a report will depend upon the information that it presents, but having clarity is more likely to shorten the report than to lengthen it.

prompt: Which of the following types of material are often included as attachments to short reports:
explanation: Supporting documents. The purpose of the short report is to present information in a concise and simple manner. Therefore, documents that support the information presented in the short report often are included as attachments rather than as parts of the main body. Readers of the report have the option to review the supporting documents or to rely solely on the information in the short report. Table of contents, title page, and conclusions and recommendations are main parts of the short report.

prompt: A memo on the bulletin board from an advertising department supervisor to staff members is an example of __________ communication.
explanation: Downward. Downward communication passes information down the chain of command to employees. This is a frequently used form of communication because supervisors must often provide general information to all workers. Horizontal communication is between persons or departments on an equal level. Upward communication moves from employees up to management. Formal communication may move in any direction; but it would be in the form of a letter, report, etc., rather than a bulletin-board memo.

prompt: Which of the following is a stock-handling activity:
explanation: Assembling shipments. Stock handling is a distribution activity that involves the loading, unloading, and handling of goods. Stock-handling activities include assembling shipments, which involves gathering together goods requested from within the company or by outside customers. Wrapping packages, checking inventory, and warehousing products are other types of distribution activities, but they are not stock-handling activities.

prompt: A short channel of distribution will probably be used by a producer that
choices: wants to share the costs of distribution.
does not have its own sales force.
explanation: Wants channel control. A producer that wants total control of the channel should use a direct channel. On the other hand, if the producer is willing to give up some control of the channel functions, longer channels can be selected. Insufficient funding, lack of a sales force, and wanting to share the costs of distribution indicate the use of longer channels.

prompt: Technology has helped improve the distribution process by utilizing __________ among channel members.
explanation: Integrated information sharing. Integrated information sharing allows near-instantaneous computer decisions related to market information, customer information, supply and inventory information, etc. The combination of all available information allows for more efficient supply-chain management. Electronic receiving, automated scheduling, and audiovisual programming do not improve the distribution process. In fact, the receiving process involves having employees check deliveries, and deciding when deliveries are scheduled.

prompt: Providing online distribution of products is one way that some businesses are able to use the distribution function to
explanation: Improve customer service. Being able to quickly deliver products to customers often results in improved customer service. Some businesses are able to do this by providing online distribution, depending on the nature of the products. For example, some magazines and newspapers distribute online versions of their publications that consumers can access free or on a subscription basis. Other businesses sell software online that customers can download immediately. The advantage of online distribution is that customers can obtain products at their convenience, which often improves service. Online distribution does not necessarily eliminate warehousing because the business may sell other products that cannot be delivered in that manner. Online distribution does not speed up the billing process or reduce the cost of advertising.

prompt: One reason a channel of distribution that has strong leadership is often able to avoid conflict within the channel is because the leader has the
explanation: Authority to demand cooperation. Strong leaders have the authority and power to influence others, and direct the actions of others. A channel of distribution that has strong leadership is often able to avoid conflict within the channel because the leader has the authority to set goals for the entire channel and demand cooperation, which reduces the possibility of conflict. The leader's authority makes it possible for the leader to assign specific responsibilities to each channel member, and persuade members to accomplish their individual tasks. When each member is cooperating and working for the good of the channel, there is less chance of conflict. It is not necessary for the leader to develop friendships. Channel leaders usually do not provide training. It is not possible to regulate change, although an effective leader will help channel members adjust to change.

prompt: A transportation service makes sure that its trucks are well maintained and driven with care. This is an example of a way to
choices: increase the number of capital goods.
explanation: Conserve the firm's capital goods. Capital goods are manufactured or constructed items that are used to produce goods and services. Trucks that are taken care of will last longer. Adding more trucks would be an example of increasing the number of capital goods. Natural resources are items that are found in nature and used to produce goods and services. Human resources, or workers, are retrained to develop new skills.

prompt: The study of how to meet unlimited, competing wants with limited resources is
explanation: Economics. This involves the process of deciding how to obtain the greatest satisfaction with limited resources. Budgeting refers to a plan for allocating funds for required expenditures. Marketing is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. The distribution function is responsible for the physical movement or the transfer of ownership of a good or service from the producer to the consumer.

prompt: A seller's market is characterized by
explanation: High demand. A seller's market is the best time for producers to sell. It is characterized by large demand, small supply, and high prices. Equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity of a good that buyers want to buy and the quantity that sellers are willing to sell at a certain price are exactly equal.

prompt: The connection between the social responsibility of an advertising agency and the community in which the advertising agency operates is that the advertising agency's social responsibility __________ the community.
explanation: Has an effect on. The social responsibility of an advertising agency affects many aspects of community life by affecting the level of employment, supporting cultural activities and educational programs, and making donations to other worthy community causes. The local community is not the only target for the advertising agency's social responsibility, but it is an important one. An advertising agency's social responsibility depends upon the advertising agency, not the community.

prompt: What is the business activity that provides information as to whether an creative boutique can afford to hire more employees?
explanation: Accounting. Accounting is the process of keeping financial records. The information in the records is used to measure and report the financial condition of a business. Management is the process of coordinating resources in order to accomplish an organization's goals. Marketing is not a business activity—it is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. Production is the process or activity of producing goods and services wanted by consumers.

prompt: Which of the following pieces of legislation was created to protect competitors from takeovers that would hinder competition:
explanation: Celler-Kefauver Antimerger Act. The Celler-Kefauver Antimerger Act was created in 1950 to protect competitors by closing the loopholes in previous legislation passed to protect competition. The Sherman Antitrust Act prevents monopolies from forming and prohibits price fixing. The Federal Trade Commission Act created a regulatory agency to monitor business activities in order to prevent unfair competition. The Robinson-Patman Act prohibits price discrimination.

prompt: When management and union leaders negotiate but cannot reach an agreement, either one may call for a(n)
explanation: Arbitrator. Sometimes management and union leaders cannot reach an agreement. When this occurs, either side may call in an arbitrator, a person who will make decisions concerning the final contract. If arbitration is called for, the decision is final and cannot be changed by the union or by management. An injunction is a court order forbidding someone from carrying out an act, such as picketing. A grievance is a disagreement between workers and employers. Probation is the time frame in which an employee is tested on the job.

prompt: It is easier for an advertising agency's account executives to develop positive client relations if the account executives understand that each client is
explanation: A unique individual. Each individual client has his or her own basic personality, and they react in different ways to account executives. The account executives should be friendly and courteous to all and adapt to each client's behavior in a positive manner. Considering each client as a possible problem is a negative approach that would probably prevent good client relations. Not all clients are in a hurry.

prompt: What is the best action for a company to take in a disaster when one of its products has been sabotaged by people outside the company?
choices: Selecting one medium and giving it exclusive rights to the story
Refusing to talk to all media
Avoiding answering any questions until all the facts about the incident are known
explanation: Being open and candid. It is important that company officials be open, honest, and direct with all inquiries. Refusal to talk with the media hurts a company's credibility and does nothing to dispel rumors. An open line of communication must be available to all consumers and media. All questions must be answered to the best of a company's ability. Withholding information or evading questions inevitably backfires.

prompt: Gaining the confidence and trust of a customer is a good technique for handling which type of difficult customer?
explanation: Suspicious. Suspicious customers may become regular customers if the salesperson can gain their confidence and trust. Disagreeable customers are often surprised and calmed by salespeople who are composed, courteous, and efficient. Domineering/Superior customers should be made to feel important and in charge, which will help them to convince or sell themselves. Slow/Methodical customers may need more action on the salesperson's part in order to close within a reasonable period of time.

prompt: Why is quick action important in handling customer complaints?
choices: Makes the situation easier to handle
Eliminates the need to investigate the problem
explanation: Pleases the customer. Taking swift action to handle a customer's complaint makes the customer feel that s/he and the problem are both important to the business. It creates an image of a business that is interested in satisfying its customers. Taking quick action does not necessarily save the manager time or make the situation easier to handle. It does not eliminate the need to investigate the problem because all complaints need to be investigated.

prompt: A business prepares an invoice for a customer who has purchased the following: four items at $31.35 each and three items at $26.95 each. If shipping costs are $19.80, what is the total amount of the invoice?
explanation: $226.05. In order to prepare the invoice, the business first needs to calculate the extensions. In this case, the customer purchased four items at $31.35 each, which totaled $125.40, and three items at $26.95 each, which totaled $80.85 ($31.35 x 4 = $125.40; $26.95 x 3 = $80.85). Then, the business adds the totals of each extension plus the shipping charges of $19.80 to determine the total invoice amount ($125.40 + $80.85 + $19.80 = $226.05).

prompt: Which of the following usually has an additional tax placed on it, beyond the regular sales tax:
explanation: Gasoline. Certain items carry excise taxes that are in addition to the regular sales tax. Items included are firearms, gasoline, telephone service, and cigarettes. Items such as small appliances, clothing, and candy are usually taxed at the regular sales tax rate, if at all.

prompt: Which employees benefit the most from a payroll debit card?
explanation: Those without bank accounts. The employees who benefit the most from a payroll debit card (paycard) are those who do not have bank accounts at all. Employees are able to use a paycard to make purchases, just as they would use a debit card—but without referencing a bank account. Direct deposit recipients do not necessarily desire a paycard because their funds are deposited in an account. Those in management and those with long employment histories do not necessarily benefit from a paycard more than other employees.

prompt: What kind of budget would a media-buying company use to plan how much it will spend on replacement or repair of equipment?
explanation: Capital budget. A capital budget, or capital expenditure budget, shows how much will be spent to refurbish or replace such capital assets as equipment, machinery, etc., as well as the source of the funds to be used. Since a business's facility and equipment require constant upkeep in order to function efficiently, the capital budget is very important to the business's success. A cash budget projects the amount of total income from all sources. An expense budget allocates the amount to be spent on each category of business expense. A sales budget estimates income from sales.

prompt: Which of the following would be considered an ethical dilemma in the personnel department of an international advertising agency:
choices: Whether the advertising agency should donate $25,000 to an animal shelter or to an orphanage
Whether the advertising agency should hold its retirement party at a nearby restaurant or at a neighboring country's banquet hall
Whether the advertising agency should pay men and women different salaries if it is operating in a country where equal pay laws don't apply
Whether the advertising agency should provide business cards for all of its associates or make them purchase business cards with their own money
explanation: Whether the advertising agency should pay men and women different salaries if it is operating in a country where equal pay laws don't apply. Ethical dilemmas occur when there is a question as to the legality as well as the morality of making a particular decision. Whether to donate money, where to hold a party, or whether to have employees pay for business cards are simply decisions that companies have to make that do not involve a moral judgment or legal issue. Choosing how to pay employees based on their gender represents both a moral and legal question and is, thus, an ethical dilemma.

prompt: Exit interviews can be conducted in each of the following ways except by
explanation: Third-party. Third-party is an ineffective way to conduct an interview because it relies on another person's interpretation of how an employee felt or the reasons why the employee has resigned. The most effective way to conduct exit interviews is in person, but they can also be conducted by questionnaire or telephone.

prompt: A tool that advertising agencies can use to orient new employees is a(n)
explanation: Employee handbook. An employee handbook provides new employees with printed information about the advertising agency that the employee can read and refer to when s/he has questions about the business. Employee handbooks usually include basic information such as company history, hours of operation, benefits, and company policies. Providing employees with handbooks reduces the amount of time that must be spent in orientation sessions. An exit interview is a discussion with an employee who is leaving the company. A performance appraisal is an evaluation of the employee's job performance. A job applicant provides a prospective employer with a copy of his/her resume, which outlines his/her work experience and educational background.

prompt: The type of training in which schools and businesses cooperate to provide on-the-job practice for learners is known as
explanation: Internships. In an internship, classroom instruction is combined with on-the-job training in a variety of scheduling arrangements. Group training may involve a small group of employees or the entire work force and is useful for explaining theory or reasons for a specific operation. Outside courses include training from various educational institutions or correspondence courses providing training in very specific areas or degree programs. Workshops or seminars may be external or internal sources of training on the premises or at an outside location.

prompt: Which of the following is an effective way to implement the solution to an employee complaint and obtain immediate employee feedback:
choices: Posting a notice on the bulletin board
Sending letters to employees at home
Explaining the problem in an employee publication
explanation: Conducting a staff meeting. Staff meetings will enable management to interact with and get feedback from employees about the complaint. The other alternatives are effective techniques for communicating with employees, but they do not enable managers to interact with employees.

prompt: Which of the following is a situation in which the use of increasingly more severe penalties would probably be inappropriate:
choices: An employee fails to meet her/his sales quota.
An employee is tardy in reporting to work.
An employee pilfers goods from the business.
An employee accepts personal telephone calls while at work.
explanation: An employee pilfers goods from the business. Certain serious offenses, such as employee theft, may be exempt from progressive discipline. This is because a stronger penalty is warranted with the first infraction than is normally administered for other, less serious, violations. Tardiness and personal use of a company's telephone are less serious actions that can be corrected through the use of progressive penalties. Failing to meet a sales quota is not a violation, per se. It may indicate that additional training is needed to help the salesperson meet company expectations.

prompt: In an advertising agency, who coordinates a client's project with agency team members in the creative department, production department, and media-planning department?
explanation: Account executive. The account executive is the liaison between the client and the advertising agency. The account executive is involved in the day-to-day activities to ensure that all team members (creative, production, media planning) are completing their tasks on time and within budget. A bookkeeper handles the agency's accounts payables and accounts receivables. The art director is the person who is in charge of the art design team. The broadcast manager manages the team that completes tasks related to television and radio projects.

prompt: Which of the following is one way that advertising agencies use marketing information:
choices: To gather data about current trends
explanation: To determine what consumers want. One way that advertising agencies use marketing information is to determine what their clients want and need in order to develop products that will be successful. Marketing information tells advertising agencies about their clients' preferences, opinions, likes, and dislikes. Advertising agencies use this information to determine their what clients want so they will develop and provide appropriate client services. Advertising agencies obtain marketing information by gathering data about current trends and sending questionnaires to clients. Advertising agencies periodically evaluate their research techniques in order to make sure they are obtaining useful information.

prompt: Facts about demographic shifts, the competition, and product demand gathered to solve a business's problem are examples of
explanation: Primary data. Primary data are collected specifically for the problem or project at hand. They may be used to solve a problem, to explore an opportunity, or for any other purpose useful to the business. Marketing research is the systematic gathering, recording, and analyzing of data about a specific problem. Data analysis is the process of evaluating information. A situation analysis is a determination of a firm's current business situation and the direction in which the business is headed.

prompt: Internet technology enables marketing-information managers to
explanation: Search vast online databases. The technology that combines computing and telecommunications created the Internet, which enables marketing-information managers to search vast online databases. The Internet is the interconnection of thousands of computers and computer networks all over the world. Marketing-information managers can use their computers to access the Internet and search the electronic databases that contain enormous volumes of information. Searching online is much faster and more efficient than conducting library research because the computer is able to locate large amounts of specific information in a matter of seconds. Marketing-information managers do not use the Internet to manipulate research findings, modify departmental statistics, or create sampling procedures.

prompt: Advertising agencies often maintain current demographic information to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to
explanation: Reach the target market. Demographic information is information about the physical and social characteristics of the population such as age, marital status, income, etc. Advertising agencies often maintain current demographic information to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to reach the target market, which is the particular group of customers a business seeks to attract. By monitoring demographic information, advertising agencies are able to detect changes in the target market and revise the marketing strategy to remain effective. Demographic information does not help businesses to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to analyze the economy, negotiate with suppliers, or purchase new equipment.

prompt: Listing the number of respondents who answered "agree," "no opinion," or "disagree" to each question on a marketing questionnaire is an example of
explanation: Tabulation. In many cases, processing marketing information involves tabulating the results. Tabulating is counting the number of respondents who answered each question with one of the possible answers. For example, if 100 people answered a questionnaire, researchers need to know how many of them agreed, disagreed, or had no opinion about the questions. Also, tabulating helps researchers to determine if some people did not answer all the questions, which might have an effect on the accuracy of the information. Listing the number of respondents who answered a certain way to each question is not an example of deviation, proportion, or association.

prompt: Which of the following is a consideration in the place element of marketing:
explanation: Choosing distribution channels. The place element of marketing focuses on considerations in getting the selected product in the right place at the right time. Some of the other place considerations are storage, transportation, inventory handling and control, and choice of specific outlets to offer the products. Sales promotion is an aspect of the promotion element. Extending credit is a consideration of the price element. Warranties and guarantees are considerations in the product element.

prompt: The process of dividing the total consumer market into smaller groups of potential customers is known as
explanation: Market segmentation. Markets can be segmented according to the demographic, geographic, psychographic, or behavioral characteristics of the customers or potential customers. Mass marketing is designing products and directing marketing activities in order to appeal to the whole market. Loyalty response is exhibited by consumers who favor a particular brand over all others. The process of dividing large work efforts into smaller units is called division of labor.

prompt: An advertising agency identifying consumers who meet certain demographic criteria and then developing ads aimed specifically at those consumers is an example of
explanation: Target marketing. Target marketing is the identification and selection of markets for a business or for a product. When an advertising agency identifies consumers based on certain demographic criteria, such as age, income, and education, and then develops ads aimed specifically at those consumers, the agency is involved in target marketing. The value of target marketing in advertising is that specific groups of consumers are more likely to respond positively to ads that appeal to their unique characteristics. Identifying consumers who meet certain demographic criteria and then developing ads aimed specifically at those consumers is not an example of composite selling. Goal setting is the ability to visualize, set, and focus on achieving business objectives. Product positioning is a product-mix strategy in which a business creates a certain image or impression of a product in the minds of consumers.

prompt: Why is it important for businesses to analyze the competition on a regular basis?
choices: To compete on an ethical basis
explanation: To determine ways to compete. Businesses need to analyze the competition on a regular basis in order to understand their competitors and to develop ways to effectively compete in the marketplace. The competitive environment changes constantly. Therefore, businesses must keep up to date with what their competitors are doing in order to remain successful. Businesses do not analyze the competition in order to eliminate competitors, understand laws regulating competition, or compete on an ethical basis.

prompt: In which of the following situations should a media-buying company increase its sales forecast for the coming year:
choices: Cost of supplies will increase by 2%.
Inflation rate is expected to drop by 1%.
Wages and salaries will remain the same.
explanation: Inflation rate is expected to drop by 1%. Changes in the economy affect sales and, thus, sales forecasting. When the economy improves for any reason, such as a 1% decrease in inflation, the clients' available income tends to increase, which means there is more money available for advertising and other promotion. A media-buying company should consider economic changes when forecasting sales and raise its expectations for the coming year if it thinks its clients will be able to buy more of its services than in the past. A media-buying company might consider lowering its sales forecast if the cost of supplies will increase by 2% or the client base will decrease by 5%. The sales forecast might stay the same if wages and salaries are expected to remain the same.

prompt: Which one of the following is a method that a manager might use to control marketing planning:
explanation: Environmental monitoring. Environmental monitoring involves checking assumptions to see whether any of the marketing plan's basic assumptions have changed. Gamesmanship refers to management actions aimed at improving the manager's performance. Behavioral displacement occurs when the behaviors encouraged by control are inconsistent with company goals. Operating delays are an unfortunate consequence of manager-control efforts.

prompt: Creative boutiques evaluate the performance of their marketing plans by comparing the results with the original marketing
explanation: Objectives. Objectives are goals that a business seeks to reach with its marketing plan. Creative boutiques evaluate the performance of their marketing plans by comparing the results with the original objectives. A creative boutique would consider its marketing plan to be successful if its performance meets or exceeds the objectives. If the objectives were not met, a creative boutique would take corrective measures to solve the problem. Marketing strategies are plans of action for achieving marketing goals. Priorities are the order of importance of your activities. Alternatives are other options or ways of accomplishing tasks.

prompt: What do advertising agencies often do with the information obtained as a result of conducting a marketing audit?
explanation: Plan corrective action. Conducting a marketing audit is worthwhile only if advertising agencies use the information obtained to develop a plan to correct problems. The purpose of a marketing audit is to identify problems or techniques that are working effectively with the intention of making adjustments to improve the advertising agency's marketing performance. Once advertising agencies have the information, they need to use it to improve or revise their marketing efforts. The information obtained as a result of conducting a marketing audit might suggest that an advertising agency revise or update its existing pricing strategy or change its advertising approach. Advertising agencies do not use marketing audits to organize current supply inventory.

prompt: An example of how modern technology is impacting and changing the advertising industry is the placement of
explanation: Banner ads on the Internet. The technology of computers and global communication is opening up a new avenue to advertisers that want to reach a worldwide market. The development of the Internet has created a new advertising medium. Now, many agencies are expanding their services to include developing and placing banner ads and other types of advertising spots on the Internet. The involvement of advertising on the Internet will continue to grow as this new medium evolves. Billboards, television commercials, and public-service announcements are types of advertising that have been in existence for a long time.

prompt: Jeff constructs a web site for his advertising agency using a web-based computer program that allows him to build his site online by using a step-by-step process. This web-based computer program is an example of a(n) __________ tool.
explanation: Design. Design tools make it easy for a small businesses (e.g., advertising agencies) to automate the look or layout of their e-commerce sites, which eliminates the need for a professional programmer. Authoring tools generate HTML and allow users to design web pages in "what you see is what you get" fashion, similar to word processing. Unilateral and editing are not types of online computer programs that help people design their web sites.

prompt: Which of the following do many advertising agencies include on their web sites in order to obtain feedback from clients:
explanation: Return e-mail option. Many advertising agencies provide a feedback option on their web sites that enables clients to e-mail the business concerning problems or to ask questions. The return e-mail option is an effective method of providing customer service as long as the advertising agency responds in an appropriate amount of time. A portable document format allows users to view files created by another operating system. An electronic file attachment allows a user to send an attachment with an e-mail message. Computer programming code is used to create software, web pages, etc.

prompt: Full-service advertising agencies should keep records of accidents and injuries in order to identify unsafe situations and to
explanation: Correct hazards. Full-service advertising agencies should keep a running log or record of work-related accidents in order to identify patterns or trends in workplace accidents. Full-service advertising agencies use this information to correct the hazardous or unsafe situations and help prevent accidents from occurring. Full-service advertising agencies do not keep accident reports for the purpose of completing paperwork. The accident reports may answer certain questions about the incident, although that is not their primary purpose. Accident reports are not needed in order to administer first aid.

prompt: In an advertising agency, the first step in the industrial purchasing process is to
explanation: Determine the business's need. The advertising agency must first determine that there is a problem or need for a product or type of product. Then the advertising agency can determine the product desired, search for and choose a supplier, and negotiate terms.

prompt: An advertising agency's employees who never take company supplies or equipment, such as pens or tools, for their own use help the advertising agency to
explanation: Control expenses. Employees can play a role in controlling business expense by not appropriating the advertising agency's property. The advertising agency should explain to employees that controlling expenses helps the advertising agency to increase its profits. External theft occurs when items are stolen by persons outside the company or shoplifted by customers.

prompt: Which of the following would not be part of the responsibilities of an advertising agency's maintenance department:
explanation: Selling goods. Selling goods involves planned, personalized communication intended to influence purchase decisions and enhance future business opportunities. It is not a maintenance function. The maintenance department makes periodic inspections and repairs of various machines, escalators, elevators, air conditioners, and heating systems in order to keep them in good working order. The maintenance department also makes seasonal or permanent changes to the advertising agency's physical layout, as the agency requires.

prompt: Which of the following should you do when you fail to reach a goal:
explanation: Find out what went wrong. Not all goals can be achieved. When you don't reach a goal, look for the reason; don't blame it on someone else. You may need to adjust your goal or set a new one, but don't give up goal-setting because of a single failure. Congratulate yourself when you reach a goal.

prompt: Tom's letter to the advertising agency's interviewer was most impressive because he had included
choices: a short statement as to why he would be the best individual for the position.
the names of high-ranking people currently employed by the company.
a sincere plea to be hired for the position.
a thank-you, confirming interest in the job, and follow-up information.
explanation: A thank-you, confirming interest in the job, and follow-up information. All of this information should be included in the letter. Including the names of high-ranking people in the advertising agency does not guarantee a position. A short statement as to why you would be the best individual for the position is important but should not be the only item. It is never wise to plead for a position.

prompt: How should a job seeker respond to a business's help-wanted advertisement that asks applicants to send a resume?
choices: By sending a resume and a cover letter
By sending the resume as requested
By calling on the business in person
explanation: By sending a resume and a cover letter. Businesses often include in their help-wanted advertisements a request that job applicants send the business a resume. The job applicant should comply with this request, but s/he should also send a cover letter with the resume. The cover letter, or letter of application, lends a personal touch to the resume and helps to "sell" the job applicant to the business. Businesses ask for resumes in their ads in order to save time. They do not want applicants to call on the phone or in person. Instead, they screen applicants by reviewing the resumes and interviewing only those applicants who seem best qualified for the job.

prompt: Which of the following is a self-regulatory service provided by some professional advertising organizations:
choices: Reviewing ads to identify possible violations
Editing ads to meet industry standards
Developing systems to obtain quality illustrations
explanation: Reviewing ads to identify possible violations. Some professional advertising organizations offer the service of reviewing ads for possible violations such as being deceptive or inaccurate. The value of this type of self-regulatory service is that it gives the advertising agency the opportunity to revise the ad before it is released to the public. By providing self-regulatory services, professional advertising organizations help agencies to prepare truthful and ethical ads that avoid violating governmental regulations and prevent lawsuits. Professional advertising organizations do not edit ads to meet industry standards, establish procedures for developing ads, or develop systems to obtain quality illustrations.

prompt: What would be the most appropriate pricing strategy for a business in a small town where unemployment has skyrocketed and the economy is in a downturn?
explanation: Flexible pricing. Flexible pricing means that a business adjusts prices up or down according to changes in economic or other factors that affect consumer spending. High-level pricing in economic hard times would reduce sales. Odd-cents pricing is used to give the illusion that a price is slightly lower than it is. For example, many consumers perceive $4.99 as closer to $4.00 than to $5.00. Below-cost pricing would mean selling products for less than what the business paid for them, which would lose money for the business.

prompt: What technological advancement has allowed consumers to collect the most information for price-comparison shopping?
explanation: Internet. More than a new way to take orders and deliver merchandise, the Internet has proven valuable to consumers as a source of information and a new way to compare prices and products. The Internet provides customers with more information about more products in less time than they can obtain from making telephone calls or by reading the newspaper or a catalog.

prompt: To help determine the selling price for one of its services, an advertising agency would calculate the service's
explanation: Break-even point. This is the point at which the revenue from sales of a service will cover the advertising agency's costs of performing the service and the expenses of business operation. The advertising agency does not make a profit until it has reached the break-even point. Assessed value is the value placed upon property for tax purposes. Depreciation is a decrease in value of something through use and/or passage of time. Opportunity cost is the benefit that is lost when scarce resources are used for one purpose rather than another.

prompt: Businesses should set their selling prices at a level that will
choices: be lower than that of competitors.
be equal to the cost of goods.
ensure a high percent of profit.
explanation: Cover expected markdowns and expenses. Businesses can prevent markdowns and expenses from cutting into their net profit by setting prices that include allowances for markdowns and expenses. Setting the original selling price equal to cost would result in a loss for the business. Undercutting competitors' prices may be possible in some cases but is unwise if it reduces profits. Setting prices that will ensure a high profit may result in prices that are too high to foster sales.

prompt: The reason Pepsi has used Shaquille O'Neal in its commercials is to appeal to younger audiences. This is an example of product
explanation: Positioning. Product positioning is the consumer's image or impression of a product as compared to that of competitive products. Product positioning directs products toward the particular segment of the market to which they would have the most appeal. Product mix is the particular assortment of products that a business offers in order to meet the needs of its markets and its company's goals. Product planning is the process of developing the product/service mix in response to market opportunities. Product screening is the process of considering each idea for a new product and discarding those that seem unworkable.

prompt: What type of planned obsolescence is generally considered socially and economically desirable because the replacement product offers more benefits and/or a lower cost?
explanation: Technological. Technological obsolescence equates to significant technological improvements that result in a more effective product (e.g., CDs, from cassettes, from phonograph records). Style obsolescence refers to superficial changes to a product resulting in a new product. The new model is intended to make users of the older model feel out-of-date and encourage them to purchase the new model. This is typical in fashion merchandise. Psychological and fashion are synonymous with style obsolescence.

prompt: During the process of generating product ideas, businesses often bring together groups of employees to
explanation: Screen the possibilities. Businesses often generate many ideas, but all of them are not realistic or possible. To find the best idea, businesses often bring together groups of employees to screen the many product possibilities. The employees analyze the ideas and consider whether they are appropriate for the business and the business's current product mix. At this point, some ideas will be rejected as too risky or not profitable. Once ideas are accepted and finalized, groups of employees might organize production, review marketing techniques, and arrange distribution.

prompt: Which of the following is a source that businesses use to develop standards:
explanation: Suppliers. Suppliers are the vendors from whom businesses buy their goods and services. Often, they have contact with many companies. Therefore, they have a broad view of what is acceptable in an industry. Their broad view of the business environment can be helpful to businesses in developing their own standards. Lawyers, accountants, and advertisers usually are not involved in developing standards for businesses.

prompt: Which of the following is a way that businesses can include consumer protection as part of product/service management:
choices: Modifying products to meet consumer demand
Marketing products in new geographic areas
explanation: Testing products very carefully. Even though products have been well designed, they should also be thoroughly tested before they are put on the market. The tests should be done according to the ways in which consumers will use the products. Promoting products to target audiences is an aspect of promotion. Modifying products to meet consumer demand and marketing them in new geographic areas are aspects of product/service management but are not involved with consumer protection.

prompt: The Meredith Company carries three versions of a product made by three different manufacturers. Meredith's product mix contains three __________ of this product.
explanation: Product lines. A product line is a group of related items made or sold by one company. The product mix is the particular assortment of products that a business offers in order to meet the needs of its market(s) and its company goals. Businesses planning their product mixes often decide to handle more than one product line in order to offer their customers a choice of products/brands. An example would be a business that sells all the sizes of film produced by Kodak and Fuji. Displays, exhibits, and arrangements of products are part of visual merchandising, not elements of the product mix.

prompt: Handling complaints, processing returns, and arranging for repairs are examples of __________ services.
explanation: Post-transaction. Most businesses offer a variety of services to customers that typically occur either before, during, or after the sale. Handling complaints, processing returns, and arranging for repair are services that businesses provide after the sale and are considered post-transaction services. Customers have already purchased products but need additional service because there are problems with the products. Transaction services are offered during the sale and include services such as layaway and gift wrapping. Offering convenient hours and various types of information are examples of pre-transaction services because they take place before the sale. A sales transaction is the actual sale.

prompt: Determine if this statement is true or false: Promotion is the only element of the marketing mix that is considered when positioning a product.
choices: False, the product is the most important element of the mix considered in positioning.
True, promotion is the least expensive way to position a product.
True, promotion influences the consumers directly.
False, all elements of the marketing mix should complement the intended position.
explanation: False, all elements of the marketing mix should complement the intended position. One or two elements of the marketing mix may be primary, but all need to be coordinated for successful product/service positioning.

prompt: A good brand name should not be
explanation: A general name. A good brand name should be distinctive rather than general in order to set the product apart from competing products. It should be easy to spell and pronounce so that people will remember it. Finally, it should be adaptable to multinational marketing and the passage of time.

prompt: Why is it often difficult to evaluate the effectiveness of advertising services?
choices: Evaluating the effectiveness of advertising involves a complicated, multistep process, which is expensive and time consuming.
Only the effectiveness of print advertising can be evaluated, while broadcast advertising is usually much harder to evaluate.
Advertising does not occur in a vacuum, and results, whether positive or negative, can rarely be attributed solely to advertising.
Advertising involves the creative process and, therefore, it is impossible to evaluate its effectiveness at all.
explanation: Advertising does not occur in a vacuum, and results, whether positive or negative, can rarely be attributed solely to advertising. Whether advertising is being evaluated on the basis of recall or recognition or sales results, such evaluation can only go so far. Evaluation is usually done in artificially constructed situations that can't take into account all of the other variables that impact advertising's effectiveness—the stores, the media, and the consumers' minds. Involving the creative process and being subjective in nature makes advertising effectiveness difficult to evaluate, but some aspects of its effectiveness can be evaluated. The effectiveness of both print and broadcast advertising can be evaluated as much as any advertising can be. Both offer their own advantages and limitations in the evaluation process. There is no single process for evaluating the effectiveness of advertising; there are many techniques—some are complex, and some are simple. Each technique varies in terms of time and expense.

prompt: Can any brand name be selected and used by a business?
choices: Yes, a business can use any name it wants to use.
Yes, brand names cannot be owned by a business.
No, the name must be legally available for use.
No, the name must be registered before it can be used.
explanation: No, the name must be legally available for use. The business needs to make sure the brand name is not the property of another company since it is illegal to use another company's brand name. Brand names can be registered with the federal government in order to protect them, but this is not necessary in order to use a brand name that is legally available.

prompt: The promotional tool that is not paid for by the business that receives it is
explanation: Publicity. Publicity is promotion provided by the media at no cost to the business. The business may, however, incur expense in its efforts to obtain publicity. There are expenses involved in personal selling, advertising, and sales promotion.

prompt: A company's sponsorship of a free cholesterol test for the community is an example of __________ promotion.
explanation: Corporate. Corporate promotion is another term for institutional promotion; the goal of corporate promotion is to create a certain image in the eyes of consumers. The company's sponsorship of a free cholesterol test gives the public the idea that the business is concerned with the welfare of the community. Primary and secondary promotion are forms of product promotion, which is concerned with selling a good or service.

prompt: Personal selling would be a cost-effective form of promotion for which of the following products:
explanation: Scanner. Personal selling is the form of promotion that uses planned, personalized communication in order to influence purchase decisions and enhance future business opportunities. Certain industrial and retail products with hidden or complex features require technical explanation by skilled salespeople. The garden rake, soft drink, and newspaper are not complicated or sophisticated products. Consequently, personal selling would not be cost effective for these products.

prompt: What is one way that advertising agencies are using technology to promote their services?
explanation: Web-site advertising. The World Wide Web (WWW) is a vast collection of interconnected sites and files accessible through the Internet. Many advertising agencies have sites on the Web and use these sites as a way of advertising and promoting their services to clients. Some advertising agencies buy advertising on related web sites and set up the ads in such a way that users can be transported to the advertising agencies' home pages by clicking on the ad. Online-media planning, electronic scheduling, and digital processing are not ways that advertising agencies use technology to promote their services.

prompt: Advertisers often try to increase the impact of their ads by using such primary colors as
explanation: Red, yellow, and blue. Primary colors are the basic colors on the color wheel. Color is often used to increase the impact of advertising. Color ads that are reproduced by a four-color process are printed in red, yellow, and blue inks. Black, white, and gray are neutral colors. Green, violet, and orange are secondary colors.

prompt: What type of headline promotes an advantage to the reader of using the advertised good or service?
explanation: Benefit. The type of headline used depends on the type of message the headline writer wants to send. Stressing the benefit, or advantage, of using a good or service is an effective headline writing technique. Consumers often are attracted to advertising headlines that promise benefit and value, and will continue to read the remainder of the ad. Information and news headlines provide new information. Command headlines tell readers to do something.

prompt: The reason that an advertiser selects a simple typeface in a large size for a print advertisement is to
explanation: Increase readability. Selecting the typeface for an ad is very important because type helps attract reader interest. If the type is small or difficult to read, people may avoid the ad. A simple typeface in a large size increases readability. However, some ads may contain specialty type that is designed for emphasis rather than readability. A simple typeface in a large size would not be used to create a distraction or develop contrast in an ad. Simple type often is used to provide necessary information and does not convey an emotion.

prompt: Which of the following situations is an example of a business using telemarketing for promotional purposes:
choices: A digital communications company calls customers to announce new options in wireless service.
An interactive kiosk allows customers to design and personalize their greeting cards.
A community bank gives a customer a personal CD player when s/he opens a checking account.
A local car dealer places a full-size advertisement in several community newspapers.
explanation: A digital communications company calls customers to announce new options in wireless service. Telemarketing is defined as an advertising medium that utilizes telephone service to promote a product either by phoning customers or providing a number for them to call. When a company calls customers to advise them of new service options, the company is engaging in telemarketing activities. A kiosk is a stand-alone structure located in a public place that is designed to provide information and sell products. When a community bank gives a customer a gift upon opening a checking account, the bank is engaging in sales promotion activities. A car dealer who pays to place information in newspapers is using print advertising to promote products.

prompt: Sending an e-mail newsletter to all customers/clients on a monthly basis is an example of
explanation: Frequency. Timing involves two components: frequency and delivery time. Frequency refers to how often the e-mail is sent out. It could be daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly, or any time in between. E-mail newsletters are often sent monthly to provide important information to customers/clients. Conformity involves sending e-mails that fit a standard format and have the same look and writing style. Quantity is volume or amount. Security involves issues of privacy and trustworthiness.

prompt: One feature of a well-designed shopping cart is the ability to
explanation: Store billing information. A shopping cart is an electronic catalog that allows customers to view products, read product descriptions, obtain prices, select items to be purchased, and review their choices. One feature of a well-designed shopping cart is the ability to store billing information so that customers do not have to re-enter the information on subsequent purchases. A well-designed shopping cart is easy for customers to use and minimizes the amount of personal information that they need to enter each time they visit. A shopping cart is not intended to obtain customer feedback, build product awareness, or evaluate online promotion.

prompt: A magazine advertisement printed on two pages that face each other is called a
explanation: Spread. A spread is a magazine advertisement that is printed on two facing pages. The cost is usually the same as that of two, one-page ads. A gatefold is a magazine ad printed on magazine pages which fold out to present a single ad. A split run is running two different ads for the same product in different editions of the magazine. A bleed page is an advertising page without a white border. The ad extends to the edges of the page, or bleeds off the page.

prompt: Which of the following often limits the impact of any single advertisement:
explanation: Clutter. Clutter, the existence of a large number of advertisements within a medium or vehicle, can limit the impact of any single advertisement. Advertisers should choose vehicles with less clutter, often those with fewer competitors' advertisements. A budget is an estimate of what income and expenses will be for a specific period of time. Prestige is a reputation based on achievement and renown. Audience is the group of consumers who observe the advertisement.

prompt: What is a major consideration for advertising agencies when deciding whether to place ads on television and radio?
explanation: Ratings. Ratings indicate the size of the viewing or listening audience. This is an important consideration when deciding whether to place ads on television and radio. Advertising agencies want to place ads on network stations, cable stations, or radio stations that have high ratings and also appeal to their target market. The intention is to have as many people as possible see or hear the ad. Circulation and zoning are considerations when placing ads in magazines and newspapers. Traffic is a consideration when placing outdoor advertising such as on billboards.

prompt: Even though some advertisers don't devote much time or effort to their signage, why does signage involve some of the most important promotional decisions a business will make?
choices: It can keep customers away forever if produced in colors or typestyles that frighten them.
It can cause automobile accidents if too distracting, and the advertiser is usually held liable.
It creates the first impression and should make a memorable statement about the business.
It affects the environment around it and should be neat and tasteful.
explanation: It creates the first impression and should make a memorable statement about the business. Too many advertisers view signage as just another necessary expense rather than as a promotional opportunity. Signage that makes a statement may be that one thing that stays in the customer's mind! Signage does affect the environment around it, but "neat and tasteful" may be the right statement for some businesses and not for others. It is possible, but not likely, that customers could be frightened by signage; but it would probably be because of the sign's graphics, not color or typestyle. Distracting signs could perhaps contribute to poor driving and even an accident, but under what conditions the advertiser would be held liable is unknown.

prompt: Which of the following are examples of consumer-oriented sales promotions:
explanation: Bonus packs and coupons. Bonus packs are products that are specially packaged that provide customers with more items at the regular price. For example, a soap manufacturer might package its bars of soap so that customers purchase three bars at the price they normally pay for two bars. Coupons are documents distributed by a manufacturer that provide a discount to customers on certain items purchased at retail outlets. Both bonus packs and coupons are considered consumer-oriented sales promotion methods, which are geared to a product's end user. Although specialty advertising is often associated with consumer-oriented sales promotions, slotting allowances and trade shows are trade-oriented sales promotion methods.

prompt: The overall objectives of a firm's promotional plan are to stimulate product demand and
explanation: Create a positive image. Promotion is defined as a marketing function needed to communicate information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. The promotional plan is the framework for a business's promotional activities. Generally, the primary or overall objectives are to enhance or create a favorable image. Usually, a company that communicates a positive image is more likely to obtain and retain customers. By communicating information about products, images, or ideas, the company is trying to stimulate interest or create demand. Promotional mix is the combination of marketing communication channels that a business uses to send its messages (advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, and publicity). Channel members are businesses or individuals who assist in moving goods and services from the producer to the consumer. Since each consumer has different personal values, it is not possible to construct a promotional plan that considers each individual's values.

prompt: Businesses often monitor their competitors' advertising in order to develop
explanation: Similar promotions. Businesses usually analyze their competitors' advertising on a regular basis in order to find out what they are doing. If they determine that a competitor's advertising is effective, they might develop similar promotions that would appeal to their customers. Businesses develop promotions that are similar in order to take advantage of current popular trends and preferences. Each business sets its own budget based on its financial capability. A competitor's advertising usually does not reveal its operating techniques. Marketing trends are the general directions in which marketing activities are moving.

prompt: What should be the first consideration when determining the effectiveness of promotional efforts?
choices: Were the original objectives of the advertising campaign achieved?
Were pretesting and posttesting used to evaluate effectiveness?
What was the usage rate of promotional items?
Were recall and recognition testing used to evaluate effectiveness?
explanation: Were the original objectives of the advertising campaign achieved? Evaluation involves determining to what extent the advertising plan's original objectives have been achieved. The type of evaluation method used is based on these objectives. Pretesting and posttesting are methods used specifically to evaluate ad design and measure strengths and weaknesses of ads at different points in the development process. Recall and recognition testing are evaluation methods that can be used when questioning a sample of consumers from the target market. Use of redeemable coupons or rebate offers are good tools to use to measure the effectiveness of advertisements based on the ad's objectives.

prompt: To create visual interest in a print advertisement, a graphic designer should consider proportioning the text and graphic elements so that
choices: the graphic is placed in the middle of the page.
the text is the first element the reader sees.
one element visually dominates the page.
all of the elements are equal in size.
explanation: One element visually dominates the page. In advertising design, proportion refers to the way each element's size and shape relates to the entire layout of the advertisement. To attract the reader's attention and create visual appeal, one element should dominate the page, but it does not necessarily need to be in the center of the page. Although the visually dominant element is usually the graphic, it is not always the case. If all elements are equal in size, the advertisement may not capture the reader's attention.

prompt: An advertising agency is developing a radio commercial for a client whose target market is preteen and young teenage girls. Which of the following radio station formats would best reach this market:
explanation: Top 40. When selecting an appropriate advertising medium, an advertising agency considers the product's target audience and how it can reach the largest amount of people in the target market. Radio stations format their programming to attract certain audiences. Stations that play popular music tend to attract a young market, such as teenagers. Jazz and '70s hard rock music stations tend to attract older people. Sport talk radio tends to attract sport fans.

prompt: An example of selling an intangible product is
explanation: Creative services. Intangible products are productive activities that we pay someone else to perform. Creative services are considered intangible products because they are activities that are performed for clients that cannot be touched, smelled, tasted, seen, or heard. This may include coming up with ideas for an advertising campaign, logo, or jingle. Graphic design supplies, stock photography, and print advertisements are classified as tangible items because they can be touched, smelled, tasted, seen, or heard.

prompt: One way that a creative boutique's account executives can build client relationships through the use of effective customer service is to
choices: help the creative boutique hire productive employees.
spend a lot of time visiting with clients.
look for new techniques that benefit clients.
identify methods of saving money for the creative boutique.
explanation: Look for new techniques that benefit clients. Building client relationships through the use of effective customer service involves helping clients in as many ways as possible. One way to help clients is to always be on the lookout for new techniques that will benefit clients or information that might help clients solve problems. When account executives are proactive and go out of their way to be of service, they usually build long-term relationships with clients who appreciate the extra effort. Account executives should focus on relevant issues during meetings with clients rather than spend a lot of time visiting and carrying on casual conversations. An account executive who identifies money-saving methods for his/her employer or helps his/her employer hire productive employees is assisting the creative boutique rather than building relationships with clients.

prompt: Management may prevent any negative effects of selling policies by ensuring that the policies do not
choices: address both internal and external factors.
explanation: Restrict the salesperson's normal authority. Salespeople should be able to sell their products without being restricted by petty rules. Selling policies should provide a framework for salespeople by defining the sales job for that particular business and ensuring uniform action by salespeople. Selling policies do not need to be in writing, but they should be flexible and address the internal and external factors that can affect them.

prompt: One way that salespeople often are able to gain the trust and confidence of their customers is by
explanation: Behaving ethically. Ethics are the basic principles that govern a salesperson's behavior. Salespeople who are ethical treat customers fairly, present their goods and services truthfully, and provide as much information as possible. Ethical salespeople usually are able to gain the trust and confidence of their customers because the customers feel that the salespeople are being honest with them. As a result of their ethical behavior, salespeople often are able to develop long-term relationships with customers. Entertaining lavishly, lowering prices, and making promises they cannot keep are not ways of gaining a customer's trust and confidence.

prompt: One of the benefits of obtaining selling information from company promotional materials is that the salesperson will be able to use that information to
explanation: Answer customers' questions. Salespeople often use the selling information they obtain from company promotional materials to answer customers' questions. Company promotional materials, such as advertisements and brochures, usually contain valuable information that salespeople can use when customers ask questions during the selling process. Salespeople need to be well informed about the features and benefits of products because customers expect salespeople to be knowledgeable about the goods and services they sell. Salespeople usually do not order goods from vendors. Managers may suggest that salespeople read company promotional materials, which may make it easier for salespeople to discuss the products with buyers. However, these are not benefits of obtaining selling information from company promotional materials.

prompt: An inexperienced salesperson selling a nontechnical product to a customer might use a(n) __________ presentation.
explanation: Memorized. A memorized sales presentation is often effective for inexperienced salespeople because it ensures that they discuss the right information with a customer. It helps them develop confidence because they are fully prepared. Salespeople basically memorize a script that includes all the facts and details that are important to explain to a customer. This type of presentation is effective for selling nontechnical products that customers routinely buy. Experienced salespeople selling technical products often use flexible, interactive, and complex presentations to determine customers' needs, answer their questions, and provide solutions to problems.

prompt: When writing sales letters, why do salespeople often include some type of incentive?
choices: To ask customers for a special favor
To encourage readers to take action
explanation: To encourage readers to take action. When writing sales letters, salespeople often provide an incentive to encourage readers to take immediate action. Incentives might include offering a rebate or a special benefit, or encouraging customers to buy because supplies are limited or prices will go up soon. Salespeople often explain the action they want readers to take and provide the incentive to take that action in the last paragraph of the sales letter. Salespeople do not include some type of incentive in a sales letter to ask customers for a special favor, describe factual information, or present testimonials from others. However, salespeople usually include factual information in sales letters and may also include testimonials from others if appropriate.

prompt: Which management function is described in the following situation: Christy Chen, who works in a large advertising agency, determines the type of workers she needs, locates qualified applicants, selects those to be hired, and assigns the new hires to a work area.
explanation: Staffing. Staffing is the management function of finding workers for the advertising agency. When a manager staffs the firm, s/he is locating workers to fill job positions. Controlling is the management function that monitors the work effort. Directing is the management function of providing guidance to workers and work projects. Planning is the management function of deciding what will be done and how it will be accomplished.

prompt: Measuring the productivity of an advertising agency's employees is an example of
explanation: Managerial control. One part of the controlling function involves measuring the performance of the advertising agency to determine if it is achieving the established objectives. One type of performance measurement involves measuring the productivity of employees. Managers often establish standards that employees are expected to meet, such as number of items produced per hour or the quality of the items produced. Then, managers use these controls to determine if employees are performing as expected. Formal authority is the authority and responsibility officially assigned to an individual who holds a position and/or a title on an organizational chart. Leadership style is the way or manner in which a leader goes about the task of influencing others. Positional analysis is a study of the tasks and responsibilities of a position and its place in an organization.
